newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway c.bank says economy not overheating yet.
newsitem.headline: Norway c.bank says economy not overheating yet.

text.p: Norwegian central bank governor Kjell Storvik said on Wednesday the country's booming economy was not overheating at present but was heading towards such a situation.

"We are of course concerned with the development in the Norwegian economy at present because, as you say, we are heading towards a situation of overheating," Storvik said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
"But it is for the fiscal policy, it is for the state budget, to take care of that, and to try to secure the stability in the economic development," he said.
He said monetary policy in Norway was geared to securing a stable exchange rate for the crown against European currencies.
Asked if the upwards revision of inflation forecasts for 1997 meant the economy was indeed overheating now, he said:

"Not at present. Not at present. We have upgraded our inflation estimate also because there have been tax increases which go into the CPI figures in Norway and there has been a fairly strong increase in electricity prices due to the weather conditions in Norway."
He said the inflation outlook now depended partly on the outcome of wage negations in the labour market.
